title: Berg Balance échelle (BBS)
formula:
The BBS is calculated by adding the selected points for each variable:

| Variable | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sitting to standing | Needs moderate or maximal assist to stand | 0 |
| Needs minimal aid to stand or to stabilize | 1 | |
| Able to stand using hands after several tries | 2 | |
| Able to stand independently using hands | 3 | |
| Able to stand without using hands, stabilizes independently | 4 | |
| Standing unsupported | Unable to stand 30 seconds unsupported | 0 |
| Needs several tries to stand 30 seconds unsupported | 1 | |
| Able to stand 30 seconds unsupported | 2 | |
| Able to stand 2 minutes with supervision | 3 | |
| Able to stand safely for 2 minutes | 4 | |
| Sitting with back unsupported | Unable to sit without support for 10 seconds | 0 |
| Able to sit 10 seconds | 1 | |
| Able to sit 30 seconds | 2 | |
| Able to sit 2 minutes under supervision | 3 | |
| Able to sit safely and securely for 2 minutes | 4 | |
| Standing to sitting | Needs assistance to sit | 0 |
| Sits independently but has uncontrolled descent | 1 | |
| Uses back of legs against chair to control descent | 2 | |
| Controls descent by using hands | 3 | |
| Sits safely with minimal use of hands | 4 | |
| Transfers | Needs two person assistance or supervision for safety | 0 |
| Needs one person assist | 1 | |
| Able to transfer with verbal cueing and/or supervision | 2 | |
| Able to transfer safely with definite need of hands | 3 | |
| Able to transfer safely with minor use of hands | 4 | |
| Standing unsupported with eyes closed | Needs help to keep from falling | 0 |
| Unable to keep eyes closed 3 seconds but stays safely | 1 | |
| Able to stand 3 seconds | 2 | |
| Able to stand 10 seconds with supervision | 3 | |
| Able to stand 10 seconds safely | 4 | |
| Standing unsupported with feet together | Needs help to attain position and unable to hold 15 seconds | 0 |
| Needs help to attain position but able to stand 15 seconds with feet together | 1 | |
| Able to place feet together independently but unable to hold for 30 seconds | 2 | |
| Able to place feet together independently and stand 1 minute with supervision | 3 | |
| Able to place feet together independently and stand 1 minute safely | 4 | |
| Reaching forward with outstretched arm while standing | Loses balance while trying/requires external support | 0 |
| Reaches forward but needs supervision | 1 | |
| Can reach forward 5 cm (2 inches) safely | 2 | |
| Can reach forward 12 cm (5 inches) safely | 3 | |
| Can reach forward confidently 25 cm (10 inches) | 4 | |
| Pick up object from the floor from a standing position | Unable to try/needs assist to keep from losing balance or falling | 0 |
| Unable to pick up and needs supervision while trying | 1 | |
| Unable to pick up but reaches 2-5 cm (1-2 inches) from slipper and keeps balance independently | 2 | |
| Able to pick up slipper but needs supervision | 3 | |
| Able to pick up slipper safely and easily | 4 | |
| Turning to look behind over left and right shoulders | Needs assist to keep from losing balance or falling | 0 |
| Needs supervision when turning | 1 | |
| Turns sideways only but maintains balance | 2 | |
| Looks behind one side only, other side shows less weight shift | 3 | |
| Looks behind from both sides and weight shifts well | 4 | |
| Turn 360 degrees | Needs assistance while turning | 0 |
| Needs close supervision or verbal cueing | 1 | |
| Able to turn 360 degrees safely but slowly | 2 | |
| Able to turn 360 degrees safely on one side only in 4 seconds or less | 3 | |
| Able to turn 360 degrees safely in 4 seconds or less | 4 | |
| Placing alternate foot on step or stool while standing unsupported | Needs assistance to keep from falling/unable to try | 0 |
| Able to complete >2 steps, needs minimal assist | 1 | |
| Able to complete 4 steps without aid, with supervision | 2 | |
| Able to stand independently, and complete 8 steps in >20 seconds | 3 | |
| Able to stand independently and safely, and complete 8 steps in 20 seconds | 4 | |
| Standing unsupported one foot in front | Loses balance while stepping or standing | 0 |
| Needs help to step but can hold 15 seconds | 1 | |
| Able to take small step independently and hold 30 seconds | 2 | |
| Able to place foot ahead of other independently and hold 30 seconds ・Foot must completely pass the other foot ・Step width should be no wider than shoulders | 3 | |
| Able to place foot tandem independently and hold 30 seconds | 4 | |
| Standing on one leg | Unable to try or needs assist to prevent fall | 0 |
| Tries to lift leg, unable to hold 3 seconds but remains standing independently | 1 | |
| Able to lift leg independently and hold ≥3 seconds | 2 | |
| Able to lift leg independently and hold 5-10 seconds | 3 | |
| Able to lift leg independently and hold >10 seconds | 4 | |

how_to_use.why:
- Évalue divers aspects de l'équilibre au moyen de 14 tâches simples.
- Aide à prédire le risque de chute chez les patients âgés, facilitant la planification et la mise en œuvre de mesures préventives.
- Fournit une mesure quantitative de l'équilibre pouvant être suivie dans le temps.
how_to_use.when:
- À utiliser pour évaluer l’équilibre et le risque de chute chez les patients âgés, les personnes en récupération après un AVC, ou les individus présentant une altération potentielle de l’équilibre due à des troubles neurologiques.
- Utile pour les évaluations initiales et le suivi continu afin d’évaluer les changements de l’équilibre au fil du temps.
- Peut être utilisé en milieu de réadaptation pour évaluer les capacités d’équilibre d’un patient et adapter les exercices d’équilibre et la thérapie appropriés.
how_to_use.pearls:
- May not be suitable for patients who are acutely ill or have severe mobility limitations, as it requires a certain level of physical ability to complete.
- The scale may experience ceiling effects in very mildly impaired individuals, failing to capture subtle balance deficits.
- Multiple studies have identified different optimal cutoff values for assessing fall risk. This tool adheres to the original study’s cutoff of <45 to indicate a higher risk of falls ([Berg, 1989](https://utpjournals.press/doi/10.3138/ptc.41.6.304)). Other researchers have proposed various cutoff scores, typically ranging from 40 to 50. This includes specific suggested cutoff points for patients with a history of falls ([Shumway-Cook, 1997](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8996463/)) or with stroke ([Simpson, 2011](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0019431)).

next_steps.advice:
- Cet outil respecte le seuil de l’étude originale de <45 pour indiquer un risque plus élevé de chutes ([Berg, 1989](https://utpjournals.press/doi/10.3138/ptc.41.6.304)).
- Utilisez les résultats pour guider des plans d’intervention personnalisés qui ciblent l’amélioration de domaines spécifiques de l’équilibre.
- Planifiez des suivis réguliers pour réévaluer l’équilibre à l’aide du BBS afin de surveiller les progrès et d’ajuster les plans de traitement si nécessaire.
- Combinez les résultats du BBS avec d’autres évaluations (p. ex., force musculaire, analyse de la marche) pour une approche globale de la gestion du risque de chute.

more_info:
Interprétation :

| BBS | Risque de chute |
| --- | --- |
| ≥45 | Non augmenté |
| <45 | Augmenté |
